title: Adaptive sampling and customer-bridge for opaque 502 waves in Hosted API
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Several customers reported transient opaque 502 clusters during high request rate windows. Patterns show short-lived 502 bursts without consistent stack traces in runtime, often coincident with a mix of long-running streaming and high-fanout non-stream requests. This ticket implements an adaptive sampling + customer-bridge approach: (1) quickly reduce noise by sampling failing requests and capturing expanded telemetry, (2) route affected tenant flows through a customer-bridge that applies stricter admission (per-tenant QPS shaping, shorter timeouts for long-fanout), and (3) ship a targeted mitigation patch that prevents request amplification from client retries. Goal: stop customer-visible 5xx oscillations and gather enough signal to identify the underlying correlated failure (likely a short-lived async resource exhaustion in edge-to-runtime multiplexing).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Replay high-fanout mix from synthetic traffic harness (50% streaming, 50% short requests) against hosted stage environment with tenant-shaping disabled.
2) Ramp to median production peak QPS for affected region.
3) Observe transient 502 bursts on inference gateway and correlated timeouts on runtime nodes.
4) Capture telemetry via expanded sampling to validate amplification and KV-cache eviction correlation.
root_cause_summary: Preliminary traces indicate synchronized eviction spikes in the KV cache and a short-lived surge of inflight connection counts at the edge proxy, causing a small percentage of requests to error out with 502. There is no single long-lived exception in the runtime; failures coincide with request retry bursts from a handful of tenant SDKs and a rare streaming parser stall that holds connections longer than expected.
mitigation:
1) Deploy adaptive sampling agent to edge and runtime to capture 100% metadata + full trace for 0.5% of failing requests and 5% of successes for 2 hours.
2) Enable tenant-scoped customer-bridge for escalated customers: apply per-tenant QPS cap, reduce streaming default keepalive, and shorten internal timeouts for fanout requests.
3) Introduce a lightweight server-side retry-dedup token for retried requests to avoid amplification for the next release train.
4) Circulate immediate SDK guidance to customers to temporarily increase backoff windows.
rollback_plan: If adaptive sampling or bridge causes unexpected latency regressions or increased error surface, immediately revert sampling to previous rate and disable customer-bridge via runtime feature-flag. Ops runbook: toggle feature-flag, drain canary, and rollback proxy admission rules. Contact list: oncall-runtime, oncall-edge, PM for customer comms.
acceptance_criteria:
- No customer-visible 502 waves > 5 minutes during 24-hour observation window post-deploy.
- Sampling traces show consistent correlation signals (edge connection hold / KV eviction) for at least 25 distinct failing traces.
- Customer-bridge metrics: affected tenant error-rate reduced by >= 80% compared to pre-mitigation within 30 minutes.
- PRs merged with tests and feature-flag gating present.
- Postmortem draft created within 72 hours.
